questions.q: Why does dsSalesSummary's query text include "WHERE t.SalesTerritoryGroup = @TerritoryGroup" instead of just filtering the matrix visually?
options: It's a parameter-driven dataset — the filtering happens in SQL Server itself, not after the rows already arrived at the report
SSRS matrices are incapable of any client-side filtering
It has no effect — the WHERE clause is ignored at runtime
It only works if the parameter is set to Internal
questions.explain: Referencing a report parameter directly inside a dataset's query text makes it a parameter-driven dataset, so changing the parameter re-runs the query against the database rather than re-filtering cached rows.

questions.q: Why are @TerritoryID and @Year on OrderDetailByTerritory.rdl set to Internal?
options: Because that report is never opened directly with a blank prompt — it only ever receives its values from the summary report's drillthrough action
Because Internal parameters run faster than normal parameters
Because AdventureWorks2012 requires Internal parameters for any query
Internal parameters are required on every dataset regardless of use case
questions.explain: Setting a parameter to Internal removes its prompt and default entirely, appropriate for a detail report meant to be reached only via drillthrough, never opened cold.

questions.q: What does the summary matrix's drillthrough action pass to the detail report?
options: TerritoryID from Fields!TerritoryID.Value and Year from Fields!CalendarYear.Value
The entire dsSalesSummary result set as a single value
Nothing — the detail report re-prompts the user for both values
Only the SalesAmount total, with no territory or year context
questions.explain: The drillthrough action's parameter mapping sends the clicked row's TerritoryID and CalendarYear values into the detail report's matching parameters.

questions.q: What column lets the summary report's warehouse-side query resolve back to AdventureWorks2012's TerritoryID?
options: DimSalesTerritory.SalesTerritoryAlternateKey
FactInternetSales.SalesAmount
DimDate.CalendarYear
Production.Product.Name
questions.explain: SalesTerritoryAlternateKey is the original OLTP TerritoryID preserved in the warehouse dimension, which is what the dataset selects as TerritoryID and the drillthrough action passes along.

questions.q: Which chapters does this lesson's report suite combine?
options: Chapter 2 (datasets/tables/matrices), Chapter 3 (parameters), and Chapter 6 (drillthrough)
Chapter 5 (charts) and Chapter 7 (subscriptions) only
Chapter 1 (fundamentals) alone
Chapter 8 (administration) and Chapter 4 (expressions) only
questions.explain: The matrix and table layouts come from Chapter 2, the cascading and internal parameters come from Chapter 3, and the drillthrough action linking the two reports comes from Chapter 6.
